guides.title: Revit downgrade guides
guides.intro: Short answers about Revit versions: why Revit cannot save to an older version, which Revit opens which file, and how to downgrade a file.

saveAsOlder.title: Can you save a Revit file as an older version?
saveAsOlder.description: Revit has no Save As older version. Here is why, and how to get a newer Revit file into an older Revit anyway.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: No. Revit only moves files forward. When you open a file from an older version, Revit upgrades it, and every save writes the version you are running. The Save As dialog has no option for an older release, and Revit has no export to a previous Revit version.

sections.heading: Why Revit works this way
paragraphs: Each Revit release changes how a model is stored: it adds new kinds of elements, new settings and new data on existing elements. An older Revit was built before those changes existed, so it has no way to read them. Revit upgrades files as it opens them and offers no way back.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Teams rarely upgrade at the same time. A consultant on Revit 2026 sends a model to a client still on Revit 2024, and the client cannot open it. The same happens with families downloaded from manufacturers, which are often saved in the newest release, and inside one company when one office moves to a new release before another.

sections.heading: What you can do
list: Ask whether the sender kept a copy from before the upgrade. Once a model has been saved in a newer version, an older Revit cannot open it, even on the sender's computer.

Exchange through IFC. The newer Revit exports IFC and the older one can link or import it, but the result is no longer a native model: walls, families and parameters arrive as geometry with limited editing.
Export to DWG for reference. You get lines and shapes to look at or trace over, not Revit elements.

Convert the file. Revit Downgrade rewrites a Revit 2023 to 2027 file in the format of an older version, down to Revit 2022, so it opens natively. Elements the older version does not know are removed and listed for you.

head: Option
What the older Revit gets
Editable Revit elements
rows: Yes, but without the changes made since

openInOlder.title: How to open a newer Revit file in an older version of Revit
openInOlder.description: Step by step: downgrade a Revit 2027, 2026, 2025, 2024 or 2023 file so it opens in an older Revit, down to Revit 2022, for free.

sections.heading: Before you start
paragraphs: Find out which version saved the file and which version you will open it in. Revit Downgrade reads the version in your browser as soon as you add the file, so you do not need to open it in Revit first.
If several people will open the file, convert it once to the oldest version anyone uses. A file converted to Revit 2023 still opens in Revit 2024 and later, which simply upgrade it as usual.

sections.heading: Steps
ordered: Open revitdowngrade.com and add the .rvt, .rfa, .rte or .rft file.
Click the Revit version you will open it in and press Downgrade.
Wait for the conversion. Small files take about a minute, large models a few minutes for each version they go down.
Download the converted file and open it in the older Revit.

sections.heading: After opening
paragraphs: Look through the list of removed elements shown on the result page, then save the file once in the older Revit. From then on it is a normal file of that version.

sections.heading: Families and linked models
paragraphs: An older Revit also refuses to load a family or link a Revit model saved in a newer release. Convert each family (.rfa) and each linked model to the same version as the project, then load or reload them in the older Revit.

sections.heading: If something is wrong
paragraphs: If a conversion fails, or the converted file does not open, the result page lets you send the file to me so I can fix the cause. For anything else, the contact details are at the bottom of every page.

compatibility.title: Revit version compatibility: which Revit opens which file
compatibility.description: Revit opens files from its own version and older ones, never newer. A quick reference for Revit 2022 to 2027.

sections.heading: The rule
paragraphs: A Revit release opens files saved in that release or any earlier one, and upgrades them as it opens them. It never opens a file saved in a later release. The rule is the same for projects (.rvt), families (.rfa) and templates (.rte, .rft).

sections.heading: Families and links follow the same rule
paragraphs: A project open in Revit 2024 cannot load a family or link a Revit model saved in Revit 2025 or later. Families and links have to be in the project's version or older.

sections.heading: Going the other way
paragraphs: To open a newer file in an older Revit, the file has to be converted first. Revit Downgrade converts files from Revit 2023 to 2027 down to any older version from Revit 2022.

sections.heading: Upgrading takes time
paragraphs: Opening an older file in a newer Revit can take minutes for a large model, because every element is upgraded. Save the upgraded file so this happens only once.

whatChanges.title: What changes when you downgrade a Revit file
whatChanges.description: Downgrading keeps most of your model, but elements an older Revit does not know are removed. How to see what was removed.

sections.heading: What is kept
paragraphs: Most of the model. Elements that exist in both versions are written in the older format and open as normal, editable elements.

sections.heading: What can be removed
paragraphs: Each Revit release adds new kinds of elements and settings. An older Revit has no place for them, so they are removed. Styles and settings that belonged only to a removed element go with it. The further down a file goes, the more releases' additions can be removed.

sections.heading: See exactly what was removed
paragraphs: The result page lists every removed element, and you can download the list as CSV. For each kind of element it shows:
list: the class of the element, which says what kind of element it was;
how many were removed, and their ElementIds.

sections.heading: Check the converted file
list: Open it in the older Revit and read the warnings.
Use the ElementIds from the list to find the removed elements in the original model and decide whether anything needs to be redrawn.
Check the key views and sheets before you share the file.
Save it once in the older Revit.
